items.title: Amaara
items.caption: A two-piece traditional bridal look in handwoven cotton-silk. The structured bodice is boned and hand-felled, the wrapper cut on a soft bias so it falls without clinging. Worn with a gele drafted to the same head-turn.

items.title: Serwaa
items.caption: Kente-paneled shirt dress with a shirtwaist sleeve. The kente is cut on the bias and panel-set by hand so the pattern reads across the body rather than down it. Finished with corozo buttons and a split hem.

items.title: Nhyira
items.caption: Six metres of silk mikado, drafted into a cathedral train with a hand-corded bodice. The shoulder is built on a floating foundation so the line stays clean under a veil. Built over nine weeks, worn once.

items.title: Aylin
items.caption: An asymmetric evening gown in crepe, with a single draped panel falling from the left shoulder. Fully lined, invisible side zip, weighted hem so it moves as one piece of cloth.

items.title: Efua
items.caption: A power suit drafted properly — not shrunk from a menswear block. Single-button jacket, hand-padded shoulder, trousers blocked to a full break. The jacket is lined in a vintage print chosen by the client.

items.title: Maame Gyanwaa
items.caption: The dress we are asked for most. A clean slip in cotton voile with a removable belt, drafted with enough ease to sit down in. Four lengths in production, all made to measure.
